work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: CCC Part Two, Section Two, Chapter Three, Article 7 · The Sacrament of Matrimony · 1601

items.text: With your spouse establish and uphold a partnership of the whole of life, ordered toward your spouse's good.
items.quote: a partnership of the whole of life... ordered toward the good of the spouses

items.text: Be open to the procreation of children and educate the children born to you.
items.quote: ordered toward the good of the spouses and the procreation and education of offspring

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: I. Marriage in God's Plan · 1615 … 1620

items.text: Love her as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.
items.quote: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her

items.text: Leave your father and mother and be joined to your wife, so that the two become one flesh.
items.quote: 'For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one.

items.text: Hold fast to the indissolubility of the marriage bond; do not treat it as dissoluble.
items.quote: This unequivocal insistence on the indissolubility of the marriage bond

items.text: Follow Christ, renounce yourself, and take up your cross in order to live marriage in its original meaning.
items.quote: It is by following Christ, renouncing themselves, and taking up their crosses that spouses will be able to 'receive' the original meaning of marriage

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: I. Marriage in God's Plan · 1602 … 1614

items.text: Love one another with a love that images God's absolute and unfailing love.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1604
items.quote: their mutual love becomes an image of the absolute and unfailing love with which God loves man

items.text: Cling to your wife and become one flesh with her, leaving father and mother.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1605
items.quote: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife, and they become one flesh.

items.text: Be a helpmate to him, his equal and nearest, as one who represents God's help.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1605
items.quote: his counterpart, his equal, his nearest in all things, is given to him by God as a 'helpmate'

items.text: Overcome self-absorption and open yourself to the other in mutual aid and self-giving.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1609
items.quote: marriage helps to overcome self-absorption, egoism, pursuit of one's own pleasure, and to open oneself to the other, to mutual aid and to self-giving.

items.text: Do not dominate her arbitrarily; protect her from arbitrary domination.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1610
items.quote: the law given to Moses aims at protecting the wife from arbitrary domination by the husband

items.text: Be faithful and tender to one another as the books of Ruth and Tobit witness.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1611
items.quote: The books of Ruth and Tobit bear moving witness to an elevated sense of marriage and to the fidelity and tenderness of spouses.

items.text: Do not separate what God has joined; let no one put asunder the matrimonial union.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Marriage in God's Plan, 1614
items.quote: The matrimonial union of man and woman is indissoluble: God himself has determined it 'what therefore God has joined together, let no man put asunder.'

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: IV. The Effects of the Sacrament of Matrimony · 1638 … 1642

items.text: Hold fast to one another in a perpetual and exclusive bond sealed by God.
items.quote: From a valid marriage arises a bond between the spouses which by its very nature is perpetual and exclusive.

items.text: Give yourselves wholly to one another in marital consent, as before God who seals it.
items.quote: The consent by which the spouses mutually give and receive one another is sealed by God himself.

items.text: Do not seek to dissolve your marriage; keep the covenant God has made irrevocable.
items.quote: a marriage concluded and consummated between baptized persons can never be dissolved.

items.text: Help one another attain holiness in married life.
items.quote: help one another to attain holiness in their married life and in welcoming and educating their children.

items.text: Welcome and educate your children as part of your married calling.
items.quote: welcoming and educating their children.

items.text: Forgive one another and bear one another's burdens.
items.quote: to forgive one another, to bear one another's burdens

items.text: Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.
items.quote: be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ

items.text: Love one another with supernatural, tender, and fruitful love.
items.quote: to love one another with supernatural, tender, and fruitful love

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: Notes

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: V. The Goods and Requirements of Conjugal Love · 1643 … 1654

items.text: Give yourself to your spouse in total mutual self-giving, and grow continually in communion by daily fidelity to your marriage promise.
items.quote: They are called to grow continually in their communion through day-to-day fidelity to their marriage promise of total mutual self-giving.

items.text: Accord equal personal dignity and unreserved affection to your husband or wife.
items.quote: the equal personal dignity which must be accorded to man and wife in mutual and unreserved affection.

items.text: Keep inviolable fidelity to your spouse, for love seeks to be definitive and cannot be an arrangement until further notice.
items.quote: conjugal love requires the inviolable fidelity of the spouses. This is the consequence of the gift of themselves which they make to each other.

items.text: If living together becomes practically impossible, do not contract a new union, but seek reconciliation and remain faithful to the indissoluble marriage bond.
items.quote: the spouses do not cease to be husband and wife before God and so are not free to contract a new union.

items.text: Do not practice polygamy; love your spouse with an undivided and exclusive affection.
items.quote: Polygamy is contrary to conjugal love which is undivided and exclusive.

items.text: Order your married love to the procreation and education of children, and cooperate with God in this work.
items.quote: married love is ordered to the procreation and education of the offspring and it is in them that it finds its crowning glory.

items.text: As the principal and first educators of your children, hand on to them the moral, spiritual, and supernatural life.
items.quote: Parents are the principal and first educators of their children.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: II. The Celebration of Marriage · 1621 … 1624

items.text: Give yourself to your spouse through the offering of your own lives.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, II. The Celebration of Marriage 1621
items.quote: the spouses should seal their consent to give themselves to each other through the offering of their own lives

items.text: Receive the Eucharist together, uniting the offering of your lives to Christ's offering made present in the Eucharistic sacrifice, so that you may form one body in Christ.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, II. The Celebration of Marriage 1621
items.quote: by uniting it to the offering of Christ for his Church made present in the Eucharistic sacrifice, and by receiving the Eucharist
items.conflict: Reformed believers reject the Mass as a sacrifice; Christ's sacrifice was once for all (Heb 10:10-14).

items.text: Prepare for your marriage by receiving the sacrament of penance.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, II. The Celebration of Marriage 1622
items.quote: It is therefore appropriate for the bride and groom to prepare themselves for the celebration of their marriage by receiving the sacrament of penance.
items.conflict: Penance as a sacrament requiring priestly absolution is not taught in Scripture; confession is made to God through Christ (1 John 1:9).

items.text: Express your consent before the Church.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, II. The Celebration of Marriage 1623
items.quote: by expressing their consent before the Church

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: III. Matrimonial Consent · 1625 … 1637

items.text: Give yourselves freely and entirely to each other; let your consent bind you and become one flesh.
items.quote: The consent consists in a 'human act by which the partners mutually give themselves to each other'.

items.text: Consent freely, without coercion or grave fear; let no human power substitute for your consent.
items.quote: The consent must be an act of the will of each of the contracting parties, free of coercion or grave external fear.

items.text: Remain faithful to the consent you have given before the Church; let its public character protect your 'I do.'
items.quote: the public character of the consent protects the 'I do' once given and helps the spouses remain faithful to it.

items.text: Fulfill the rights and duties that marriage creates between you.
items.quote: Marriage introduces one into an ecclesial order, and creates rights and duties in the Church between the spouses and towards their children.

items.text: Fulfill the duties toward your children that marriage creates.
items.quote: creates rights and duties in the Church between the spouses and towards their children

items.text: Instruct your children in the dignity of married love, its role and exercise, and in the value of chastity.
items.quote: It is imperative to give suitable and timely instruction to young people, above all in the heart of their own families, about the dignity of married love.

items.text: Have your children baptized and educate them in the Catholic Church.
items.quote: the obligations assumed by the Catholic party concerning the baptism and education of the children in the Catholic Church.
items.conflict: Reformed believers would reject bringing up children as members of the Catholic Church, since parents must train them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord (Eph 6:4) in a biblically faithful church.

items.text: In a mixed marriage, do not let difference of confession divide you; place in common what you have received and learn from one another fidelity to Christ.
items.quote: Difference of confession between the spouses does not constitute an insurmountable obstacle for marriage, when they succeed in placing in common what they have received.

items.text: Love your nonbelieving spouse sincerely, practice the family virtues humbly and patiently, and persevere in prayer for his or her conversion.
items.quote: Sincere married love, the humble and patient practice of the family virtues, and perseverance in prayer can prepare the non-believing spouse to accept the grace of conversion.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: VI. The Domestic Church · 1655 … 1658

items.text: Be the first heralds of faith to your children by word and example.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, VI. The Domestic Church 1656
items.quote: parents are 'by word and example... the first heralds of the faith with regard to their children.'

items.text: Encourage each child in the vocation proper to him or her, fostering with special care any religious vocation.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, VI. The Domestic Church 1656
items.quote: They should encourage them in the vocation which is proper to each child, fostering with special care any religious vocation.
items.conflict: Encouraging a 'religious vocation' can lead to monastic vows or priestly celibacy; Scripture warns against forbidding marriage (1 Timothy 4:3) and upholds marriage (Hebrews 13:4).

items.text: Exercise the priesthood of the baptized in your home by receiving the sacraments, prayer and thanksgiving, holy witness, and active charity.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, VI. The Domestic Church 1657
items.quote: all members of the family exercise the priesthood of the baptized ... 'by the reception of the sacraments, prayer and thanksgiving, the witness of a holy life'

items.text: Practice fraternal love and generous, even repeated, forgiveness toward one another in the household.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, VI. The Domestic Church 1657
items.quote: Here one learns endurance and the joy of work, fraternal love, generous - even repeated - forgiveness

items.text: Open your home to single persons, especially those who lack a family.
items.citation: Catechism of the Catholic Church, VI. The Domestic Church 1658
items.quote: the doors of homes, the 'domestic churches,' and of the great family which is the Church must be open to all of them.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 1601–1666: The Sacrament of Matrimony"
heading: IN BRIEF · 1659 … 1666

items.text: Love her as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
items.quote: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the Church.

items.text: Order your marriage to the good of each other and to the generation and education of children.
items.quote: it is ordered to the good of the couple, as well as to the generation and education of children

items.text: Love each other with the love with which Christ loved his Church, and let that love perfect and strengthen your unity.
items.quote: It gives spouses the grace to love each other with the love with which Christ has loved his Church

items.text: Give yourselves to each other mutually and definitively in faithful and fruitful love.
items.quote: their will to give themselves, each to the other, mutually and definitively, in order to live a covenant of faithful and fruitful love

items.text: Do not practice polygamy; preserve the unity of marriage.
items.quote: Polygamy is incompatible with the unity of marriage

items.text: Do not divorce; preserve the indissolubility of marriage.
items.quote: divorce separates what God has joined together
items.conflict: Jesus permits divorce only for sexual immorality (Matt 5:32); Paul permits separation for desertion (1 Cor 7:15).

items.text: Be open to fertility and do not refuse the child, the supreme gift of marriage.
items.quote: the refusal of fertility turns married life away from its "supreme gift," the child

items.text: Do not remarry while your lawful spouse lives.
items.quote: The remarriage of persons divorced from a living, lawful spouse contravenes the plan and law of God as taught by Christ.
items.conflict: Scripture permits remarriage of the innocent party after adultery or desertion (Matt 5:32; 1 Cor 7:15).

items.text: Educate your children in the faith.
items.quote: They will lead Christian lives especially by educating their children in the faith.

items.text: Give your children the first proclamation of the faith and make your home a community of grace and prayer.
items.quote: The Christian home is the place where children receive the first proclamation of the faith.
